title: What Do EEG Representations Reveal? Multiview Neural Representations to Demystify the EEG-Visual Alignment
claim: Decomposing the input signal into complementary temporal, spectral and spatial views, then fusing and aligning them with image embeddings, yields richer representations.
layout: 3 parallel colored columns plus image branch, top-to-bottom flow, converging to loss
description: A wide block diagram split into an EEG Encoder panel (left, large) and an Image Encoder panel (right, narrow). At the top, an 'Input EEG' box sends arrows down into three tinted rounded panels: (A) Temporal Modeling in blue (Linear, Selective State-Space Model, Conv1D stacked layers, Temporal Projection), (B) Spectral Modeling in green (Adaptive Learnable Wavelet Decomposition splitting into X_low and X_high, two S3M blocks, Cross-Frequency Attention, concatenation circle), and (C) Spatial Modeling in pink/red (GCN, Average Pooling, Linear, GeLU, Linear). Each branch ends in an oval embedding (z_temporal, z_spectral, z_spatial), decorated with small icons: EEG waveform traces, a power spectrum plot and a brain illustration. These are concatenated, passed through a Final Projection Head to z_eeg. The image branch shows a grid of stimulus photos flowing through Vision Backbone and Image Projection Head to z_img. Both meet at a gray Loss diamond.
caption: Overview of the proposed multiview EEG–Image decoding framework. Given a multichannel EEG trial, the EEG encoder constructs complementary temporal, spectral, and spatial representations using selective state-space modeling (S3M), adaptive learnable wavelet-inspired decomposition (ALWD), and an attention-modulated graph convolutional network (GCN). These representations are fused into a compact EEG embedding, which is aligned with pretrained visual representations for zero-shot semantic decoding.
abstract: Zero-shot visual decoding from electroencephalography (EEG) aims to infer visual semantics from non-invasive neural recordings, but remains challenging due to the low signal-to-noise ratio, non-stationarity, and limited spatial resolution of EEG. Existing EEG–vision alignment methods typically model the temporal, spectral, and spatial structure of EEG separately or only partially, leaving their complementary roles in visual perception underexploited. We introduce a unified multiview EEG representation learning framework for aligning brain responses with visual semantic embeddings. Our method builds an EEG encoder that jointly models three complementary views: input-conditioned state-space temporal dynamics, learnable wavelet-based spectral decomposition for sample-adaptive frequency modeling, and attention-modulated graph learning for structured electrode interactions. The resulting multiview EEG embeddings are fused and aligned with pretrained visual representations in a shared semantic space using contrastive learning with EEG-specific regularization, enabling 200-way zero-shot visual classification. Experiments on THINGS-EEG benchmark show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, with 54.8% Top-1 and 85.6% Top-5 accuracy in the within-subject setting and 15.3% Top-1 and 45.4% Top-5 accuracy in the cross-subject setting. We further present the systematic evaluation of cross-session zero-shot EEG–image semantic decoding/retrieval, achieving 40.8% Top-1 and 78.0% Top-5 accuracy. These results suggest that explicitly modeling multiview neural structure improves both semantic alignment and generalization in EEG-based visual decoding.
